newsitem.title: THAILAND: No Thai firms face liquidity problems - BOT.
newsitem.headline: No Thai firms face liquidity problems - BOT.

text.p: The Thai central bank said on Thursday that no financial institutions under its supervision were faced with liquidity problems.

"With reference to some wire service reports today quoting the Governor as saying that a finance company is facing short-term liquidity problems, the Bank of Thailand would like to clarify that such reports are inaccurate," it said in a statement.
"No financial institution under the Bank of Thailand's supervision is facing liquidity problems," the BOT said.

"Moreover, under current volatile market conditions, the BOT has been closely monitoring the situation and is prepared to assist financial institutions in their liquidity adjustment at all times," it added.
The Thai Finance Companies Association also issued a statement earlier denying market talk that local finance firms faced a severe liquidity crunch.
"It is what the (stock) investors have interpreted, and we do not have any measures to counter the rumours," Association president Pin Chakkapak said.
The Thai stock market plunged on Thursday to a 56-month-low on worries about finance firms facing high local interest rates and tight liquidity and the current baht's weakness.
